title: GAE: Unleashing Physical Potential of VLM with Generalizable Action Expert
claim: A planner predicts sparse geometric waypoints, which a separately pretrained, reusable expert converts into dense, accurate real-time actions.
layout: Stacked top-to-bottom, three numbered VLM steps, GAE training panel, trajectory strip
description: A tall, dense diagram built from photos and annotated text. The top panel shows the VLM in three numbered steps: predict a 2D anchor point from a robot-scene image and a prompt, get a depth value from a depth map (83.1cm), then infer a 3D waypoint trajectory. Orange prompt text and magenta outputs mark inputs and predictions. A middle band shows a spline interpolation between two 3D trajectory plots. Camera space is linked to robot space, a point cloud, and an 'Inaccurate / Directly Execute' alternative. The lower panel, labelled GAE, covers large-scale data (100K real and 50K simulation), 3D annotation tools, action pretraining and PCD finetuning. Each of the last two has an Action Expert box with goal-pose and PCD inputs. A bottom strip of five robot frames carries an orange trajectory curve labelled Accurate Real-Time Manipulation. Two robot mascots label the VLM and GAE regions.
caption: The pipeline of our proposed method. Our approach begins with a VLM predicting a sparse set of 3D waypoints directly in the camera frame, preserving its vision-centric knowledge. These sparse points are then transformed and interpolated via a B-spline into a continuous and smooth pose trajectory to provide dense guidance for a low-level action expert.
abstract: Vision-language models demonstrate strong reasoning and planning abilities, yet grounding these predictions into precise robot actions remains a central challenge. Existing Vision-Language-Action methods typically entangle reasoning and action generation, leading to limited generalization. We propose Generalizable Action Expert (GAE), a task-agnostic model that converts sparse geometric plans into dense robot actions. Our approach introduces a sparse geometric interface: the VLM predicts sparse 3D waypoints representing high-level intention, while GAE maps these waypoints together with real-time point cloud observations to continuous action trajectories. GAE is pretrained on a large-scale pointcloud-trajectory dataset comprising 150k trajectories from both simulation and real-world robots. To further improve efficiency and generalization, we introduce an Action Pre-training, Pointcloud Fine-tuning (APPF) scheme that decouples learning action dynamics from geometry grounding. After pretraining, GAE is frozen and reused across downstream tasks, requiring only lightweight fine-tuning of the VLM to produce the sparse interface. Experiments show that our method achieves strong performance and generalization across diverse visual domains, camera viewpoints, and natural language instructions.
